It's becoming more and more important for scientists to understand English. It is certainly the preferred language for publication since around three-quarters of all scientific research is published in English. This trend is unlikely to change soon, but is the dominance of English in the sciences a bad thing?

Has English always dominated in the sciences? Hardly. In fact, the dominance of English is a recent thing. Back in the 1960s it was fairly common for science to be published in German, French and Russian.

So, what are the benefits for scientists of communicating mainly through English? Well, it may lead to more conversation – it allows more people in the scientific community to have their say.

  1. … but is the dominance of English in the sciences a bad thing?
